title: The leaking basket
hook: Abba Moses, asked to judge a brother, carries a leaking basket of sand: my sins run out behind me
tomorrow: a monk does every prayer on his list. what else is there to do?

segments.voice: That was the week: Wednesday and Friday, a sunrise sermon, an anvil under the hammer, Polycarp's thanks, strangers everywhere, and a vision where the church grows young as hope comes back. Now, into the desert.

A group chat can turn into a courtroom fast: screenshots as evidence, everyone weighing in, a verdict by lunch. The desert monks of Scetis had their own version. A brother has done something wrong, and they call a meeting to deal with him. They send for Abba Moses, an elder they respect. He won't come. They send again: everyone is waiting for you. So he gets up and goes. But he brings something slung over his shoulder, and it's leaving a trail.
screen: `THE GROUP CHAT COURTROOM.` → `A MEETING IN SCETIS.` → `SOMETHING LEAVING A TRAIL.`

segments.voice: This story comes from the sayings of the desert fathers and mothers, monks and nuns who went out to live simply and pray. Their elders were called abba, father, and amma, mother. Abba Moses walks in carrying a basket full of sand, and the basket leaks. Sand runs out behind him the whole way. Some tellings make it a cracked jug of water; the picture is the same. The others ask: father, what is this? And he says, in the sense of the saying: my sins are running out behind me, and I don't see them, and today I've come to judge someone else's. No speech. One basket and one sentence. And the story ends quietly: they say nothing more to the brother, and they forgive him. Look where the sand is. Behind him, out of his sight. Jesus asks the same thing with a splinter and a plank: "why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?"
screen: `ABBA AND AMMA OF THE DESERT.` · `A BASKET THAT LEAKS SAND.` · `MY SINS RUN OUT BEHIND ME.` · `THE MOTE AND THE BEAM.` · then, large: `MY OWN SINS TRAIL BEHIND.`

segments.voice: If you can, walk slowly across the room and back, and with each step picture a little sand trailing behind you, your own trail you can't quite see. Then bring to mind someone you've been quick to judge lately, and set the verdict down for the rest of the sit.
The leaking basket. Abba Moses's answer to a call to judge: walking in with his own faults trailing behind him.
Keep this one: my own sins trail behind, out of sight and still falling. Two weeks, done.

chat.meaning: Asked to judge a brother, Abba Moses came carrying leaking sand: my sins run out behind me, unseen. Hearing it, the monks forgave the brother.

Scetis.meaning: a desert where early Christian monks lived

Abba Moses.meaning: a desert elder; abba means father

amma.meaning: mother: the title for women elders of the desert

Polycarp.meaning: bishop of Smyrna, who gave thanks before the fire
